data.narrative:
Gilmour Space Technologies, an Australian Series D space and aerospace company that has raised approximately A$100M to date, is valued here against a comp universe of 5 public space equities (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private frontier-tech peers in the same sector.

Two valuation methods proved applicable. The stage-progression approach, anchoring to $100M total raised and applying a 1.5x Series D step-up multiplier, implies $150M. The peer-median method draws on four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables—Apex Space ($2.3B Series D), Varda Space Industries ($1.6B Series D), Sierra Space ($8.0B Series C), and Skyryse ($1.1B Series C)—yielding a median valuation of $1.9B, with a range of $1.1B to $8.0B. Public-comp anchoring was not applied, as Gilmour's revenue is not publicly disclosed, precluding use of the sector P/S median of 27.4x across the five public tickers.

Triangulating the two applicable methods produces a valuation range of $128M (low) to $2.2B (high), with a median of $1.0B. The wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around stage-typical step-ups and peer heterogeneity within the space sector. Key downside risks include execution risk and market timing; upside hinges on proof of commercial traction relative to the peer set.
